Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up. Short answers first: yes, co-terming is possible; we offer a few structured approaches depending on whether you want predictable unit economics or immediate capacity. Attached are two worked examples.

High level options (summary, attached in PDF + calc sheet):
1) Staged top-up (pump-up over 2 months)
   - Charged pro-rata for the remainder of the current term at the hosted rate.
   - Option to annualize at renewal: we convert consumed top-up into committed base with a one-time credit of up to 5% of the top-up spend if you commit to an annualized increase >= 25%.
2) Voucher-in-lieu (prepay credit)
   - You buy a voucher for the expected extra consumption; voucher is drawn down at the hosted rate but gives a 6% effective discount relative to month-to-month billing.
   - Voucher can be applied to annual contract at renewal toward a higher committed tier, with partial refund or roll-forward options.
3) Annualize-now (annual commitment amendment)
   - Fastest predictable economics; prorate the remainder of the year into a new annual ARR and apply tiered discounting (sliding scale, up to 12% for larger increases).

Tradeoffs to consider:
- Predictability vs. cost: vouchers/annualize give better unit economics; staged top-up is operationally light.
- Legal/PO timeline if you want a contract amendment vs. bolt-on purchase.

I've attached a sample proration calc (pioneerhealth_co-term_calc.xlsx) and a short options deck (pioneerhealth_pricing_options_v2.pdf). Can you confirm the exact expected start date and ballpark additional token volume so I can pull precise numbers? If you want, I can also put together a one-page recommendation with exact figures.

Best,
